 COMMON JUDGMENT 
 

 JUSTICE SHRI.P.Q. BARKATH ALI : PRESIDENT
Both these appeals under
section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 arise out of the order of CDRF, Thiruvananthapuram in CC.68/12 dated, January 31, 2013.  Therefore both these appeals are disposed of by a common order.  Appeal No.185/13 is filed by the first opposite party and Appeal No.304/13 is filed by the 2nd opposite party.
2.      The case of the complainants as testified by the 2nd complainant as PW1 and as detailed in the complaint before the Forum in brief is this:-
Complainants are husband and wife and are senior citizens.  They have booked flight tickets in the airlines of British Airways to travel to USA and back on visit visa.  The ticket was booked on behalf of the complainants by 2nd opposite party from the first opposite party travel agency.  The date of departure was September 8, 2009 and the date of return was March 03, 2010.  The tickets were for travelling from Banglore to Seattle in USA and back.  When they reached Seattle airport for return journey they have been informed that their tickets have been cancelled by the travelling agency and the price has been refunded to him.  Therefore complainants were compelled to purchase new tickets by paying additional amount up to Bangalore.  As they have no money to purchase air ticket from Bangalore to Trivandrum they had to travel in train.  Without their consent opposite parties have cancelled their return flight tickets which is clear deficiency of service on their part.  The claimants claimed refund of the additional amount spent for purchase of return ticket and also compensation.
3.      The first opposite party M/s Riya Travel and Tours, Thiruvananthapuram represented by its Manager, Mr.Jacob in his version contended thus:-
The Forum has no jurisdiction to try the case as the entire transaction took place outside its jurisdiction.  It is admitted that complainants have booked the tickets as alleged by them through the 2nd opposite party.  It was done by the 2nd opposite party.  Subsequently at the request of the 2nd opposite party first opposite party cancelled return ticket and refunded the value of the same to the 2nd opposite party.  The second opposite party is not an agent or sub agent of first opposite party.  Therefore there is no deficiency of service or unfair trade practice on the part of the first opposite party.  Therefore complaint is to be dismissed.
4.      The second opposite party, Mohammed Iqbal, Air International, Trivandrum remained absent before the Forum.
5.      Second complainant was examined as PW1 and Exts.P1 to P3 were marked on his side.  The Manager of the first opposite party, Travel Agency was examined as DW1 and he produced Exts.D1 and D2 before the Forum.  On an appreciation of evidence the Forum found that there was deficiency of service on the part of the opposite parties and directed them to pay the price of the return ticket purchased by the complainants ie 1855 US dollars with a compensation of Rs.50,000/-.  The first opposite party has filed the Appeal 185/13 and 2nd opposite party has filed Appeal 304/13 challenging the said order of the Forum.
6.      Heard the counsel for the appellants in both the appeals and the counsel for the complainant.
The following points arise for consideration:-
1.   Whether there was any deficiency of service on the part of the opposite parties?
2.   Whether the impugned order of the Forum can be sustained?
7.      The specific case of the first opposite party is that they have cancelled the return ticket at the request of the 2nd opposite party and that therefore there was no deficiency of service on their part.  There is no merit in the above contention.  Though second opposite party requested for cancelling the ticket, there is a duty on the part of the first opposite party to inform the matter to the complainants which they did not do.  Ext.D2 the copy of the ledger produced by the first opposite party shows that the tickets have been cancelled as per voucher dated January 26, 2010 but the complainants produced Ext.P1 which is the print out of the confirmed ticket taken on February 18, 2010 wherein it is shown that return ticket has been confirmed.  If the tickets were already cancelled on January 26, 2010 they should have updated the status of the tickets in the internet which they did not do which is a clear deficiency of service on the part of the opposite parties.  Further first opposite party has not chosen to examine the 2nd opposite party as a witness to prove that it is at his request the ticket was cancelled.  Under these circumstances we are inclined to confirm the finding of the Forum that there is deficiency of service on the part of the opposite parties in cancelling the return ticket without informing complainant.  That being so, Appeal No.185/13 filed by the first opposite party has to be dismissed.
8.      As regards Appeal No.304/13 filed by the 2nd opposite party he was set exaprte by the Forum.  The reasons stated by the 2nd opposite party for not appearing before the Forum was that he was laid up with illness and that he has misplaced the notice sent by the Forum.  But no document is produced by the 2nd opposite party to show that he was laid up with illness or misplaced the notice issued from the Forum.  That being so, we find no ground to set aside the exparte order passed against the 2nd opposite party.  Further the specific case of the first opposite party was that it was at the request of the 2nd opposite party they have cancelled the tickets.  That being so Appeal filed by the 2nd opposite party is also to be dismissed.
In the result we find mo merit in both these appeals and the same are dismissed with a cost of Rs.5000/- in each appeal.
